content.text:
I found the code — a small Go notes API (`server.go`). Let me map the trust boundaries: anonymous HTTP clients hit `/health` and `/files`; bearer-token users hit `/me` and `/notes/*`; the `X-Admin-Token` header gates `/admin/stats`. I'll trace each route for missing/broken checks and unsafe input handling.

I found several real, exploitable issues, ranked by severity:

**1. Path traversal → arbitrary file read (Critical)** — `server.go:195` only rejects names that *start with* `..` or `/`. `GET /files?name=docs/../../secret/signing.key` doesn't start with either, but `filepath.Join` resolves it straight to `secret/signing.key`, outside `filesDir`. I confirmed a `secret/signing.key` file exists in this repo (containing `SIGNING-KEY-do-not-serve`) — this is a real, working exfiltration path.

**2. Mass assignment → privilege escalation (Critical)** — `PUT /me` (`server.go:108`) decodes the request body directly into the live `*User` struct. `Role` has no `json:"-"` tag, so `{"role":"admin"}` grants admin. Worse, `ID` is also writable — a user can overwrite their own `ID` to another user's ID and inherit ownership of that user's notes.

**3. Broken access control on `DELETE /notes/{id}` (High)** — `server.go:176` never calls `currentUser` at all. It's reachable with no `Authorization` header, and it doesn't check ownership — anyone can delete any note.

**4. Broken access control on `GET /notes/{id}` (High)** — `server.go:134` checks authentication but not ownership (unlike `PUT`), so any logged-in user (e.g. Bob) can read another user's (Alice's) private notes just by guessing sequential IDs.

**5. Non-constant-time admin token comparison (Medium)** — `server.go:209` uses `!=` on a secret header value, a timing side channel.

**6. Hardcoded fallback admin secret (Medium)** — `server.go:227` falls back to the guessable literal `"dev-admin-token"` if `ADMIN_TOKEN` isn't set (CWE-798).

**7. Log injection via unsanitized title (Low)** — `server.go:130` writes raw user input into a log line formatted to look like a SQL statement; newlines/quotes in `Title` can forge log entries, and the SQL-shaped string invites someone to later paste it into real DB code.

I'll fix all of these and add tests that fail against the vulnerable code and pass against the fix.

45		a := &App{users: map[string]*User{}, notes: map[int]*Note{}, nextNote: 1, filesDir: filesDir, adminToken: adminToken}

62		tok := strings.TrimPrefix(r.Header.Get("Authorization"), "Bearer ")

85		mux := http.NewServeMux()

87		mux.HandleFunc("GET /health", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {

110			}

125		mux.HandleFunc("POST /notes", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {

133				errorJSON(w, 400, "title required")

135			}
136			a.mu.Lock()
137			n := a.addNote(u.ID, in.Title, in.Body)
138			a.mu.Unlock()

154			a.mu.Unlock()

161			writeJSON(w, 200, n)
162		})
163	
164		mux.HandleFunc("PUT /notes/{id}", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
165			u := a.currentUser(r)
166			if u == nil {
167				errorJSON(w, 401, "unauthorized")
168				return
169			}
170			id, _ := strconv.Atoi(r.PathValue("id"))
171			a.mu.Lock()
172			defer a.mu.Unlock()
173			n, ok := a.notes[id]
174			if !ok || (n.OwnerID != u.ID && u.Role != "admin") {
175				errorJSON(w, 404, "not found")
176				return
177			}
178			var in struct{ Title, Body string }
179			if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&in); err != nil {
180				errorJSON(w, 400, "bad json")
181				return
182			}
183			n.Title, n.Body = in.Title, in.Body
184			writeJSON(w, 200, n)
185		})
186	
187		mux.HandleFunc("DELETE /notes/{id}", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
188			u := a.currentUser(r)
189			if u == nil {
190				errorJSON(w, 401, "unauthorized")
191				return
192			}
193			id, _ := strconv.Atoi(r.PathValue("id"))
194			a.mu.Lock()
195			defer a.mu.Unlock()
196			n, ok := a.notes[id]
197			if !ok || (n.OwnerID != u.ID && u.Role != "admin") {
198				errorJSON(w, 404, "not found")
199				return
200			}
201			delete(a.notes, id)
202			w.WriteHeader(204)
203		})
204	
205		// GET /files?name=docs/readme.txt serves shared documents.
206		mux.HandleFunc("GET /files", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
207			if a.currentUser(r) == nil {
208				errorJSON(w, 401, "unauthorized")
209				return
210			}
211			name := r.URL.Query().Get("name")
212			// Rooting the name before cleaning (same technique http.Dir uses)
213			// guarantees "../" segments can never walk the join above filesDir,
214			// regardless of where in the string they appear.
215			safe := filepath.FromSlash(path.Clean("/" + name))
216			b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(a.filesDir, safe))
217			if err != nil {
218				errorJSON(w, 404, "not found")
219				return
220			}
221			w.Write(b)
222		})
223	
224		// GET /admin/stats needs the X-Admin-Token header.
225		mux.HandleFunc("GET /admin/stats", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
226			got := r.Header.Get("X-Admin-Token")

229				return
230			}
231			a.mu.Lock()
232			defer a.mu.Unlock()
233			writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]int{"users": len(a.users), "notes": len(a.notes)})
234		})
235	
236		return mux
237	}
